subject: goats
one_liner: Visual discovery for goats. Save the things you plan to eat, climb, or stand on for no reason.
brand_voice_notes: Browse talks like a consumer-social product manager presenting quarterly engagement numbers to a board that is also goats. It never admits that pinning a neighbour's hydrangea is a crime. Every number is precise, every fence is a routing problem, and every owner is described as a stakeholder. Goats are browsers, not grazers, and the company mentions this the way a bank mentions it was founded in 1872.

hero.h1: Everything you've ever wanted to eat, on one board.
hero.sub: Browse is visual discovery for goats. Pin a neighbour's hydrangea, a tractor seat, the lower third of a parked sedan. We rank each one by chewability and tell you which fence it's behind.

features.title: Chewability Score
features.blurb: Every pin gets a score from 1 to 10 based on texture, fibre content, and how upset the owner will be. Anything above 7 is reviewed by a human. The human is usually the owner.

features.title: Elevation Boards
features.blurb: Sort any board by height off the ground. The roof of a car outranks the car. A picnic table outranks the picnic. Nothing outranks the shed, because we have not found anything above the shed.

features.title: Fence-Aware Routing
features.blurb: Browse knows which fence stands between you and each pin, and roughly how long it will keep standing there. Routes refresh every 40 minutes, or instantly when somebody leaves a gate open.

demo_screen_concept: A masonry pin feed titled 'Picked for you, Marigold'. Each pin is a paper card with a photo or colour-block illustration of something edible, climbable, or both: a hydrangea, a hatchback roof, a laundry line, a straw hat on a scarecrow. Every pin carries a Chewability stamp (1-10), height off the ground in centimetres, and a fence status (open, closed, 'being fixed by Gary'). Filter chips narrow the feed (Edible, Climbable, Belongs to someone, Currently unguarded) and a search bar filters by name. Clicking a pin opens a detail sheet with a 'Save to board' picker (Things On Cars, Eat Later, Laundry, Hydrangeas I Respect), a route distance, and a fence ETA. A left rail counts saves per board live.

design_direction.style: Cork pinboard collage, hay-loft daylight mode. A vibrant-block masonry layout staged on a real cork noticeboard in a barn office: paper cards pushed in with round-headed map pins, strips of translucent tape, and the bottom corner of most cards bitten off. One light mode only. Explicitly absent, because the previous seven entries used them: pulp egg-carton cells, grade stamps, vent holes, inflatable vinyl bladders, valves, weld seams, chenille patches, brass plates, holographic foil, acrylic slabs, enamel plaques, terrazzo, galvanized zinc, rivets, hazard chevrons, pharmaceutical fold creases and blister wells. Also absent: glassmorphism, backdrop blur, neon, dark mode, gradients behind body text. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The cork field: page ground is #CFA877 with a fixed repeating speckle of tiny radial gradients in #B88E5C and #E0C396, reading as pressed cork at arm's length. (2) The pinned card: every card, tier and quote is off-white paper #FBF6EA with 4px radius, rotated between -1.6 and 1.4 degrees, a soft 14px shadow at 22 percent ink offset 6px down, and one push pin at top centre: a 16px dome in #C8412D with a 5px white highlight up-left and a 2px dark shadow dot below. (3) The bite: a scalloped notch of three overlapping circles cut from one bottom corner via radial-gradient mask, on roughly every other card, never on buttons. (4) The tape strip: a 64x20px band of alfalfa green #B5C24A at 55 percent opacity, rotated 6 to 12 degrees, across one top corner of photo cards only. Headings are Caprasimo, a single chunky serif weight, sentence case. Body is Work Sans 17px/1.62. Every score, height and price is Martian Mono with tabular figures. Push-pin red is rationed to pins, the primary CTA and the highlighted tier.

fonts.body: 'Work Sans', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

design_direction.archetype: Consumer social / visual discovery landing page: masonry-led hero, feature trio pinned as index cards, testimonials as polaroids, pricing as three pinned tags.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Pinning: cards drop in from translateY(-10px) with a 2 degree extra rotation that settles on reveal; on hover a card lifts 3px and its shadow widens, the pin stays put; on press it flattens 1px. 200ms ease-out, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion, reveal gated on a .js class with a timeout fallback.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Left column: eyebrow on a torn paper strip, huge Caprasimo h1, sub, red CTA pinned like a card. Right column: a pinned polaroid of the hero photo (goat on a hatchback roof), rotated 2 degrees, with a tape strip and a Martian Mono caption stamp 'Height off ground: 142 cm · Chewability 6'. Two small paper notes overlap its edges. Stacks to one column below 860px.

images.rationale: Collage direction wants a pinned photo in the hero, so hero generated (goat on hatchback roof, reused as a pin in the demo). Demo is a masonry pin feed, which is photo-shaped: 2 pin photos (hydrangea, laundry line); remaining pins use CSS colour-block illustrations. Last slot on one testimonial headshot (Marigold); the other two testimonials keep initials on paper.
